summary: The literature supports the team's process numbers, but the BOAK pass at S$98.7/tCO2e in final_v1_7 is not robust. The deck and final_v1_7 are two incompatible models (100,000 Nm3/h, 0.585 Mt, 43.5 MMSCFD against 130 MMSCFD, 0.899 Mt, 34.0 MMSCFD). Four evidence gaps drive the economics. (1) T&S of S$23.2/t comes from a Netherlands EOR assumption, while ERIA/GCCSI shows Singapore transport alone at about US$43 to 86/t. (2) The ledger has no MEA regeneration heat term (S$23 to 34/t), and no reference applies MEA to shifted syngas. (3) Gas saving is 35.2% in INL but 18.8% in Ahn and Lee 2026, which would take BOAK to about S$148/t. (4) The 34.0 MMSCFD figure depends on tail-gas recycle and the 5.7 MWe N2 unit that the drafts exclude. A favourable offset exists: the 600 MWth size scaling is a team assumption, and removing it lowers BOAK by S$55/t. Combining the unfavourable items additively gives about S$168/t BOAK and S$128/t 10-OAK (screening, my calculation). Citation fixes needed: deck slide 26's US$2,900 to 9,200/kW is the AP1000, not the Xe-100 (X-energy states about US$3,600/kW NOAK); Sheng 2023 gives 90% only as a LEDS scenario assumption and says hydrogen is not included; Cho 9.35 is verified as direct emissions from 33 US plants, but the 35/65 split is not in the abstract and the full text could not be opened. The split matches INL's 35.2% gas reduction rather than any stream split; IEAGHG's stream split is 56/44. External facts are verified: NDC 45 to 50 Mt, carbon tax S$45 for 2026 to 2027, INIR tentatively 2027, NMDP 26 Oct 2026, about 100,000 Nm3/h for the SOXAL unit, 2025 LNG US$12.09/MMBtu and FX 1.3065. The NUS-NTU Master's comes from the Minister's lecture and is a target, not part of NMDP. The western island page does not mention nuclear.

conflicts.detail: Deck: 100,000 Nm3/h, 66,927 t/y, 0.585 Mt/y, S$31.5M/y gas, US$80/t CCS, US$420M reactor. final_v1_7: 130 MMSCFD, 97,946 t/y, 0.899 Mt/y, S$94.8M/y gas, S$23.2/t T&S, INL reactor basis. 176.8 MWth applies only at 130 MMSCFD; at 100,000 Nm3/h it is 120.8 MWth.
conflicts.resolution: Pick one basis and regenerate the deck. INL 130 MMSCFD is the consistent one.

conflicts.topic: Deck gas saving against its own CO2 ledger
conflicts.detail: Slide 25 uses 43.5 MMSCFD, the 725 C ROT case, while the 6.08 kg/kg process CO2 matches the 925 C case of 34.0 MMSCFD (5.95 kg/kg). At 34.0 the deck saving is S$64.8M/y, not S$31.5M/y.
conflicts.resolution: Use 34.0 MMSCFD for a 925 C design. final_v1_7 already does.

conflicts.detail: S$23.2/t derives from EUR 10/t (NL EOR, ZEP 2011). Deck uses US$20/t (US basis). ERIA/GCCSI gives Singapore transport about US$43 to 86/t before storage; IEAGHG 2022 gives EUR 54.6/t. BOAK fails above S$25.5/t.
conflicts.resolution: Central case should rest on SE Asian evidence. BOAK at S$60/t is S$120.1/t.

conflicts.detail: INL 35.2% against unabated SMR. Ahn and Lee 18.8%, also with tail-gas recycle and 900 C helium. Implied generated CO2 5.95 against about 7.30 kg/kg (my calculation).
conflicts.resolution: Keep INL central for flowsheet consistency, show Ahn as a sensitivity. BOAK about S$148/t on Ahn's percentage.

conflicts.detail: Drafts exclude tail-gas handling and the 5.7 MWe unit, yet 34.0 MMSCFD exists only because all fuel gas is recycled with cryogenic N2 removal (TEV-961 PDF pp14 to 15). IEAGHG 2022 and Ahn also tie furnace removal to tail-gas rerouting.
conflicts.resolution: Bring recycle inside the boundary or stop using 34.0 MMSCFD.

conflicts.detail: Capture capital is IEAGHG Case 1A activated MDEA, utilities are INL Selexol, but the design is 30 wt% MEA. No MEA reboiler heat appears in the ledger or the 206.0 MWth screening value.
conflicts.resolution: Add an explicit regeneration heat term, or change solvent basis.

conflicts.detail: Deck labels 35% furnace and 65% process. IEAGHG stream split is 56/44, feed and fuel split is 86/14. 35% equals INL's net gas reduction. Abstract has no split; full text not accessible.
conflicts.resolution: Keep 9.35 as the baseline. Rewrite the split as the net effect of nuclear heat plus tail-gas recycle, sourced to INL.

conflicts.detail: Deck and report cite Sheng for industry-standard amine capture at 90% on syngas. Sheng is a scenario assumption for gas power and industrial gas, with hydrogen not included.
conflicts.resolution: Cite IEAGHG 2022 (90% minimum, p56; Table 5 p72) and disclose that 90% at scale is undemonstrated (p13).

conflicts.detail: Slide shows US$9,200/kWe and US$1 to 2bn for one 200 MWth unit. The cited source applies US$2,900 to 9,200/kW to AP1000; US$1.1 to 1.2bn is a four-pack NOAK. US$5,250/kWe has no source found.
conflicts.resolution: Replace with the INL basis or the correct X-energy figures, labelled as a management estimate.

conflicts.detail: final_v1_7 summary states S$64/t, the 10-OAK value; body shows BOAK S$98.7/t and FOAK S$169.3/t. Capital uses overnight cost with no IDC, owner's cost or contingency, while IEAGHG TCR/TPC is 1.30.
conflicts.resolution: Headline the range by stage. Add at least IDC, which is +S$10 to 20/t on BOAK.

conflicts.detail: Design needs 925 C ROT. Xe-100 and HTR-PM are 750 C; HTTR 950 C is a 30 MWt test reactor. final_v1_7 Table A10 shows the 750 C case fails at every stage, yet the cost basis is a generic reactor figure.
conflicts.resolution: State plainly that the case depends on a reactor not commercially identified.

conflicts.detail: Reactor is 210 MWth in deck and v1.7, 230 MWth in the 31 Oct revision, and INL's equivalent is 178.8 MWt. Slide 9 captions the western island 'proposed location (gov.sg)' while v1.7 uses Jurong Island; gov.sg names power generation only and does not mention nuclear.
conflicts.resolution: Align rating and site. Use Jurong Island as a concept and treat the western island as a future option with no nuclear designation.

decisions.question: Which single scale basis should the deck and report share?
decisions.why: Abatement, heat duty, gas saving and reactor rating only reconcile on one basis. Moving from 100,000 Nm3/h to 130 MMSCFD changes tonnes by 1.46x.
decisions.default: INL 130 MMSCFD (97,946 t/y), stated as 1.46x the SOXAL unit.
options: SOXAL 100,000 Nm3/h with heat scaled to 120.8 MWth

decisions.question: What central T&S tariff should the economics use?
decisions.why: BOAK crosses S$100/t at S$25.5/t, so this input decides pass or fail for BOAK.
decisions.default: Central S$60/t, with S$23.2/t as the low case and an ERIA-based high case.
options: S$23.2/t retained with a stated caveat
S$112/t or more for a stand-alone chain

decisions.question: How is MEA regeneration heat supplied and costed?
decisions.why: It is 68 to 79 MWth, absent from the ledger and from 206.0 MWth, and worth S$23 to 34/t.
decisions.default: Keep 30 wt% MEA, add an explicit heat term net of 24.5 MWth export steam.
options: Supply from reactor and raise rating
Supply from recovered process heat with evidence
Switch to MDEA or Selexol to match the references

decisions.question: Is PSA tail-gas recycle inside the boundary?
decisions.why: The 34.0 MMSCFD gas saving and the low residual CO2 both rely on it.
decisions.default: Inside the boundary, restoring 5.7 MWe (220.4 MWth screening requirement).
options: Purge route with purge emissions counted
Outside, with gas use recalculated without recycle

decisions.question: Which gas-saving basis is central?
decisions.why: INL and Ahn differ by S$44M/y, or S$49/t.
decisions.default: INL 34.0 MMSCFD central, Ahn 18.8% as a named sensitivity.

decisions.question: Which maturity stage is the headline abatement cost?
decisions.why: S$64/t, S$99/t and S$169/t tell different stories, and the rubric asks for a defensible cost with uncertainty.
decisions.default: Report BOAK with the FOAK to 10-OAK range and do not headline S$64/t alone.

decisions.question: What capital basis applies to the reactor?
decisions.why: Overnight cost omits IDC, and the 0.6 size scaling from an unverified 600 MWth reference moves BOAK by S$55/t.
decisions.default: Add IDC, keep n = 0.6, and label 600 MWth as a team assumption.
options: Overnight plus IDC and owner's cost

decisions.question: Should the report name a reactor product or remain generic?
decisions.why: Xe-100 is 750 C and the draft shows the 750 C case fails at every stage, so naming it undercuts the 925 C basis.
decisions.default: Generic 925 C HTGR, with Xe-100 used only for safety-case analogy.

gaps: Cho full text not accessible (HTTP 403), so any combustion and process split in the paper is not verified.
ETC Exhibit 3.8 seen only on the deck slide image; the source PDF exceeded the fetch limit.
Original GCMD report not opened; BCG's page used for the US$141 to 174/t boundary.
No published Singapore-to-Indonesia project T&S tariff found; storage cost for Singapore in ERIA Table A.2 not read because it is an image.
No published FOAK cost for a single Xe-100 unit found; X-energy S-1 not read in full.
The claim that INL's US$6,000/kWe reflects a 600 MWth reactor is not verified; reference [46] not opened.
ALSG total hydrogen capacity and actual output of the 2011 SMR not found.
Official Singapore gas price in S$/GJ and MAS October 2026 USD/SGD average not found; about 1.28 is from aggregators.
DICE reboiler duty and PCC-only capital line not extracted; INL/RPT-24-77048 SMR range not accessible (HTTP 403).
Ahn SI not available, so HTGR capital cost and T&S treatment are unknown.
Full NDR 2026 speech text not read; only the gov.sg page and secondary reports.
